name: inkscape-layer-rotated-quiz-plate
exporter: Inkscape 1.3 - Save As > Plain SVG, layers kept
story: A question band made the way anybody makes one: a tall box drawn portrait and turned flat - with the rotation on the LAYER, which is where Inkscape and Figma put it.
idioms: transform="translate(...) rotate(-89.5)" on the <g inkscape:groupmode="layer">, and no transform at all on the rect inside it
the text carrying the counter-rotation so the words read level while living in the turned frame
inkscape:label naming the layer and a plain id on the shape
an XML declaration with standalone="no", two-space indentation, the inkscape namespace declared on the root
whyThisMatters: Every rotated file in the corpus carries its rotation on the SHAPE, which is what Illustrator writes. Inkscape and Figma write it one level up, on the layer or frame group, and that is the level the runtime reads its scale from - so the whole corpus agreed with the code by accident. Read as the matrix entry "a" rather than as the length of the frame's x basis vector, a rotation of 89.5 degrees reports 0.0087 screen pixels per drawn unit instead of 1: measured on this file before the 2026-09-04 fix, one line was handed 123,760 units of room inside a plate 1,240 units wide. A budget nothing can overflow means the ladder never wraps and never shrinks, so the words run straight out of the plate and off the frame - the worst possible answer to a long value, on a shape a student makes by rotating a box.
